path_exercised: each serving process composed by build_served_app: start_serving (anchor read, launcher when no claimant waits, one claimant consumed), executor with fence, runtime watch and fresh volatile cache, durable jti replay, periodic watch refresh in the lifespan, drain and retire on shutdown

DurableExecutionService: profile compatibility, RFC 8785 canonical identity, keyed idempotency digests, read-only step-10 lookup, bounded wait for an active duplicate

cases.detail: 200 with replayed false, validated against the frozen response schema, settled at the synthetic charge. One provider request.

The one permitted retry (same body and key, fresh token and request ID) returns 200 with replayed true, the new request ID, and the original execution ID, output, usage, profile release and cost. Provider requests remain one.

A second process from the same anchor runs the launcher, takes a higher fence and has an empty cache. The duplicate returns 409 idempotency_recovery_unavailable with the completed execution and its settled receipt, no Retry-After, and the new process makes no provider request. One record exists.
Ten minutes after admission by the cache's clock the body is gone and the duplicate returns 409 idempotency_recovery_unavailable. No second provider request.

Activating a successor release of the same profile and route makes the duplicate 409 execution_invalidated with the completed execution and receipt. Eligibility is decided before the cache is read. No second provider request.

With no active release, the duplicate returns 409 execution_invalidated, and a new key returns 503 privacy_route_unavailable with no execution or cost and creates no record. No second provider request.
An active route and rate quarantine makes the duplicate 409 execution_invalidated. No second provider request.

An unusable candidate commits failed and returns 502 provider_response_invalid with the failed execution and settled receipt; the duplicate returns the same stored error and receipt. One provider request.

A duplicate arriving while the original is dispatched waits its own one-second attempt ceiling (asserted between 0.9 and 5 seconds), then returns 409 request_in_progress with Retry-After 1, the dispatched execution and a pending_reconciliation receipt, while the original is still held in the provider. The whole case runs on one event loop, so an answer while the original is held shows execution no longer blocks the loop; with the calls moved back onto the loop the same test fails. One provider request.
Once the watch closes, both a new key and a duplicate return 503 state_store_unavailable with no execution or cost; nothing is admitted and no provider request is made.

cases.case: every serving configuration holds the cache
cases.detail: DurableExecutionService refuses an executor without a replay cache, and an executor without one answers a completed duplicate with IdempotencyRecoveryUnavailable, never an empty success.
A duplicate that begins waiting while the original is dispatched returns 200 replayed true with the original execution ID and output once the original completes inside its wait. One provider request.

cases.case: revocation after dispatch, before the completed commit
cases.detail: Run for a profile revocation and for a privacy-policy revocation. The revocation commits while the provider holds the request; the completed commit's recheck sees it and commits failed with execution_invalidated, settled at the reported charge, with no response digest and no cached body. The original returns 409 execution_invalidated with the failed execution and settled receipt; the duplicate returns the same. One provider request.

cases.case: revocation arriving during the completed commit
cases.detail: With the completion transaction past its recheck and still open, apply_revocation is started and observed still blocked on the subject lock 4 seconds later. The completed commit lands first, the original is delivered with 200, and the revocation then commits and ends replay: the duplicate returns 409 execution_invalidated. With the revocation's lock removed the same test fails, on two runs.

cases.case: revocation committed inside settlement, before the recheck
cases.detail: A revocation committed inside the settlement transaction, after its record locks but before its recheck, is seen by the recheck, which reads after taking the lock. The candidate is suppressed with execution_invalidated.

Activating a successor profile release through activate_release while the provider holds the request lets the connected original finish with 200 under its pinned release; the duplicate then returns 409 execution_invalidated. One provider request.

A revocation committed inside the dispatch transaction, before its recheck, aborts the admitted record: failed, execution_aborted, settled at zero, reservation released. The request returns 409 execution_aborted with that receipt and no provider request is made.

tiamat_runtime reads only its own caller scope's signed releases under RLS and is refused FOR SHARE and UPDATE on the authority tables, which is why the fence is an advisory lock rather than a row lock.

build_served_app starts through the launcher, serves 200, refreshes the watch from the anchor on its interval while serving, and on shutdown retires its fence without blocking the gate. A second process from the same configuration starts through the launcher at a higher fence and answers the earlier key with 409 idempotency_recovery_unavailable.

When the lifespan's refresh reads an unverifiable anchor, the watch closes with recovery_anchor_unverifiable and blocks the gate; the next request returns 503 state_store_unavailable, nothing is admitted and no provider request is made.

suite.full_suite: 1429 passed, 283 skipped; the skips are older vertical-slice tests that need a different integration database
suite.mutation_checks: Removing the completed-commit recheck fails 3 eligibility cases; removing the revocation's lock fails the arrival-during-commit case on two runs; moving execution back onto the event loop fails the bounded-wait case.

interpretations_for_review: Accepted by Lyra: a profile with no active release answers a duplicate with 409 execution_invalidated and a new key with 503 privacy_route_unavailable, as a documented fail-closed interpretation for an otherwise authorized profile.
A cached body that disagrees with the ledger's execution ID or digest is answered as idempotency_recovery_unavailable.

A revoked head for a pinned subject suppresses even when the pinned release is a superseded predecessor, because apply_revocation can only target the current head. This is conservative in the direction RC1 requires.
Issuer is not filtered in the revocation check, so a mismatch between the ledger scope's issuer and the authority issuer can only over-suppress.
A duplicate whose record is still active when its wait ends, but whose lease has already elapsed, returns state_store_unavailable, since lease expiry belongs to the reaper.
known_gaps: Gate 3 prerequisite, before any real provider call: a provider result without an exact charge leaves the record dispatched for the lease reaper, which resolves it to outcome_unknown, and the request returns state_store_unavailable. settle_terminal has no failed-with-pending_reconciliation path for provider_response_invalid.

The served profile set is still configured in memory (ServedProfiles). The fence reads revocation from the signed-authority tables, so a profile that was never activated there is not refused at admission. Wiring admission to require an active signed release is the follow-up that closes that split.

build_served_app composes a process from a ServedConfiguration. There is no loader yet that builds that configuration from the deployment's trust package, secrets and signed authority, and no provider transport exists, so nothing is deployable to staging traffic until those are decided.
The bounded wait polls the ledger every 100 ms per waiting duplicate.

eligibility_design.decision: No new counter. The security/privacy eligibility named in RC1 section 11 is realised as the pinned profile and privacy-policy releases, evaluated at dispatch and at the completed commit against signed_releases.state and release_heads.head_state. A revoked pinned release, or a revoked head for its subject, suppresses; a superseded one does not, which is the RC1 split between revocation and routine replacement.
eligibility_design.why_not_release_heads_eligibility_genera: release_heads.eligibility_generation increments on routine successor activation as well as on revocation, so comparing against it would suppress connected originals that RC1 acceptance item 80 requires to be delivered.
eligibility_design.ordering: A transaction-scoped advisory lock per authority subject (environment, caller, realm, release type, subject). apply_revocation takes it exclusively before writing; dispatch and the completed commit take it shared before reading. The serving role cannot take FOR SHARE on the authority tables without UPDATE, which it must not hold.
eligibility_design.execution_records_eligibility_generation: unchanged and not used by this fence
eligibility_design.advice: An independent read-only design review (Fable) recommended this over a scope-level counter; its focused tests were adopted, with shared rather than exclusive locks on the serving side.
